#### Windowed against temporal — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** Why a windowed join and a temporal join are two different operations rather than two configurations.

`windowedJoin()` compares two **stream** rows, so neither is authoritative and the pair exists only once both have arrived. `tableAsOf(et)` has the line that defines a temporal join: `if (r.et > et) { continue }` — skip versions later than the row's own event time, which is why it needs the table's **history**.

Step 3 is the contrast in one case: click 0 gets NONE immediately from the temporal join, while the windowed join needs a retraction to deliver its match with impression 7.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

Both operands are stream rows, so neither is authoritative — the pair exists only if BOTH have arrived, which is why the buffer and the wait exist. 5 pairs come out of this loop, and nothing here says when any of them may be published.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — the temporal join probes a TABLE as of the row's own time</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch09-kinds-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: the temporal join probes a TABLE as of the row&#39;s own time" width="980">

The `continue` skips table versions later than the row's own `et` — that is the "as of" semantics, and it is why the lookup needs the table's HISTORY rather than its current value. For click 3 the answer is 11, determined the moment the click arrives.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — so a row before the table existed gets NONE, not a wait</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch09-kinds-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: so a row before the table existed gets NONE, not a wait" width="980">

Click 0 at 12:00:01 precedes every impression, so `any` stays false and the result is NONE — **immediately**, not after a wait. Compare the windowed join, where the same click's match with impression 7 requires a retraction to deliver.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and that is the whole difference: one waits, one does not</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch09-kinds-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and that is the whole difference: one waits, one does not" width="980">

`wWaits` is "both watermarks" and `tWaits` is "nothing". Read the heap rows: `pairs` holds 5 matches of which 2 are never published, while `enriched` holds all 5 rows, complete. Windowing a lookup imports the first column's problems for no benefit.
